facts.statement: The species Rinconsaurus caudamirus was described in 2003 based on three partial skeletons.
facts.quote: The type species, Rinconsaurus caudamirus, was described by Calvo and Riga in 2003, and is based on three partial skeletons.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus was a titanosaur sauropod that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Rinconsaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous in what is now Argentina.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus was an unusually slender sauropod compared to others of its kind.
facts.quote: Rinconsaurus was an unusually slender sauropod.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rinconsaurus were discovered in 1997 near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils of Rinconsaurus were discovered in 1997 by Gabriel Benítezin strata belonging to the Bajo de la Carpa Formation near Rincón de los Sauces, in the Neuquen province of Argentina.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus is distinguished by unique tail vertebrae with bony processes.
facts.quote: The authors noted derived traits unique to the genus, including distinctive tail vertebrae with bony processes.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus is classified as a titanosaurid sauropod.
In 2007, some researchers assigned Rinconsaurus to the clade Aeolosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2007, Casal et al. assigned Rinconsaurus, Gondwanatitan, and Aeolosaurus to the Aeolosauridae, a proposed stem-based clade of titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus is proposed to form a clade called Rinconsauria with Muyelensaurus, though this classification is not yet widely accepted.
facts.quote: Rinconsaurus would form a smaller clade Rinconsauria with Muyelensaurus. It remains to be seen, however, if this classification will receive widespread acceptance.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus lived approximately 83 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Unlike many other sauropods, Rinconsaurus was a slender animal.
facts.quote: Rinconsaurus a diferencia de muchos otros saurópodos, era delgado.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus fossils were discovered in 1997 by Gabriel Benítez near Rincón de los Sauces in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Rinconsaurus fueron descubierto en 1997 por Gabriel Benítez cerca de Rincón de los Sauces, en estratos pertenecientes a la Formación Bajo de la Carpa, en la Provincia del Neuquén en Argentina.

facts.statement: Researchers noted unique characteristics in Rinconsaurus, including distinctive tail vertebrae with bony processes.
facts.quote: los autores notaron características únicas en este animal, incluyendo las distintivas vértebras caudales con procesos óseos.

facts.statement: The generic name refers to the discovery site Rincón de los Sauces, while the specific name means "amazing tail" due to unusual vertebrae shapes.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se refiere a Rincón de los Sauces, donde se descubrieron los fósiles, mientras que el epíteto específico, caudamirus, significa "cola asombrosa", en referencia a la inusual forma de las vértebras especialmente una extraña secuencia de procoelos, vértebras anficoelas, opistocoelas, biconvexas y finalmente procoelas nuevamente mostradas por un individuo.

facts.statement: In 2007, some researchers assigned Rinconsaurus to the tribe Aeolosaurini within the subfamily Saltasaurinae.
facts.quote: En 2007, Casal et al. asignó a Rinconsaurus, Gondwanatitan y Aeolosaurus a Aeolosaurini, una tribu dentro de la subfamilia Saltasaurinae.

facts.statement: In 2007, Calvo, González Riga, and Porfiri erected a clade named Rinconsauria for Rinconsaurus and Muyelensaurus.
facts.quote: Alternativamente, en 2007 Calvo, González Riga y Porfiri erigieron un clado para este dinosaurio junto a Muyelensaurus dentro de Saltasauridae llamado Rinconsauria
Rinconsaurus, like all sauropods, was an herbivore.

facts.statement: Fossilized dung from titanosaurids suggests Rinconsaurus ate a diet including palms and grasses, leading to speculation about co-evolution with grasses.
facts.quote: discoveries published in 2005 revealed an unexpectedly wide range of monocotyledons, including palms and grasses (Poaceae), including ancestors of rice and bamboo, which has given rise to speculation that herbivorous dinosaurs and grasses co-evolved.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus possessed pencil-chisel-like teeth with sharply inclined wear facets.
facts.quote: Teeth found in association with Rinconsaurus have been described as "pencil-chisel-like teeth" and had sharply inclined wear facets.

facts.statement: Rinconsaurus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)
